sections.h2: Three ways to sell a Bryan house
sections.html:
In Bryan you can list with an agent, handle the sale on your own, or accept cash. How long the house can sit and what condition it is in should drive the choice. Listing brings cleanup, open houses and a closing that waits on the buyer's lender. A cash buyer skips those steps and discounts the price for repairs and risk.

Selling without an agent means you set the price, field the calls and work the contract through a title company yourself. That saves a commission, but it only works for someone at ease screening buyers and reading a contract line by line.

Before choosing, jot down two figures: the likely net from a listing once costs and waiting are counted, and the cash offer with a firm closing date.

The city has more than 93,000 people and shares Brazos County with College Station and Texas A&M. Long-time families, university staff, students and renters all shape who shows up to buy or lease a house here.

Rail service came in 1867 and Bryan incorporated November 29, 1871. Its oldest houses stand around historic downtown, and an inspector will start with the wiring, plumbing and foundation of any of them. Electric service comes from the city's own Bryan Texas Utilities, so call the utility office about final readings and transferring service on closing day.

Brazos Central Appraisal District puts a value on each parcel, and every taxing unit that serves it then sets its own rate. The calendar below decides who owes what at your closing.

Yearly sequence for Brazos County property tax
WindowWhat happens
January 1Assessment date for the parcel
April through MayNotices of appraised value mailed in several runs between April 15 and June 1
May 15 or 30 days after noticeLast day to protest the value
July through SeptemberCity, county, school and special districts set their rates
October and NovemberThe assessor-collector mails bills

You can reach the district at 4051 Pendleton Dr. in Bryan or 979-774-4100. Tax for a given year is secured as of January 1, and whatever is unpaid after January 31 goes delinquent. If you close in fall or winter, that year's bill is typically still open, and the settlement statement must say who pays it. Rates shift annually, so ask the Brazos County tax office for each unit's current figure.

Living in the house lets you claim the residence homestead exemption, which removes $140,000 of value for school taxes. Older and disabled owners receive more school relief and a tax ceiling. Ask Brazos CAD whether a service-connected disability earns a veteran a separate exemption.

  • Exemption applications go to the district by email, and phones are answered weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
  • Zoom details for appraisal review board hearings are posted on the district's tax process page.

Disputes over value go before the appraisal review board, which has its own email at the district. Certain properties, undivided-interest ownership among them, can't use the online appeals portal. If yours is one, phone the district well ahead of the deadline.

sections.h2: Selling a house that was a short-term rental
sections.html:
Rent a Bryan home, apartment or garage unit for 30 days or less and it counts as a short-term rental. Hotel occupancy tax of 7 percent applies to the gross rent, including cleaning and pet charges.

  • Returns are filed through the GovOS portal, due monthly by the 20th of the next month.
  • Owners who owe under $500 a month or $1,500 a quarter can file quarterly.
  • A quarter with no bookings still needs a zero return.
  • To close an account, email the GovOS support address with the closure date and reason.

File your last returns before handing over the keys, so no tax balance follows you. The city's fiscal services office answers questions at 979-209-5080. Tell any buyer whether guests are already booked for future dates.

sections.h2: Inherited, behind on payments or rented?
sections.html:
Each of these has its own timeline.

If the owner has died, a title insurer will ask for a court order or a sworn affidavit before it covers the sale. The state law library outlines three routes, and each takes different paperwork.

Behind on the loan? The servicer's default letter starts a 20 day window to catch up. A sale notice then has to go up at least 21 days before the courthouse auction, and a sale before that date can protect your equity.

If a tenant lives there, the first step is a written notice to vacate, usually three days, and a court filing comes next. An as-is buyer takes over wherever the case stands.

Unpaid tax sticks to the land. A buyer inherits the problem unless it is paid off, so an old balance gets settled out of your sale proceeds. Phone the Brazos County tax office for an exact payoff figure before you weigh offers, and subtract it in your head from every number you hear. Anything left open after January 31 is delinquent and keeps growing, which is a reason to ask early.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Brazos County
sections.html:
The Brazos County clerk serves as recorder, and the deed for a Bryan lot is filed there. Before it records a conveyance, the clerk needs either a notary's acknowledgment or two witnesses.

The Texas courts' 2023 clerk manual sets one fee for the first page, a smaller one per added page, and several extras. The clerk can give you the current total. Usually the title company records the deed and mails you a copy.

sections.h2: What to line up before a cash closing
sections.html:
Collect your newest tax bill, a mortgage payoff figure, any lease, and rental tax filings if guests booked the house. Heirs bring probate or affidavit paperwork, and an heir who isn't on the deed must also show the appraisal district an ownership interest before claiming an exemption. With these papers in hand, a buyer can name a price and a closing date quickly. Students and other renters near the university may be living in the house under a lease, and if so, the lease is one of the first documents a buyer will request, along with the date it ends.

After you sign an offer, the title company searches for liens and open taxes while you fix the closing date and ask the utility office for final meter readings. At closing, tax proration and any loan payoff come out of your proceeds, a notary witnesses the deed signature, and the clerk files it. Keep the settlement statement with your tax records and cancel your own insurance afterward.

faqs.q: How fast can a Bryan house sale close?
faqs.a: With clean title a cash sale can finish in a few weeks, since no lender signs off. Listing takes longer because the buyer's loan and appraisal set the clock. Either path slows down for an unprobated estate or an open lien.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax when a Bryan house sells?
faqs.a: The sale year is normally split between buyer and seller on the settlement statement. Earlier unpaid years must be cleared at closing because that lien stays with the land. Call the Brazos County tax office for your balance.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bryan house that is listed on Airbnb?
faqs.a: Yes. File your hotel occupancy tax returns first, because the city requires monthly or quarterly reports on short-term rent. Tell buyers if future dates are already booked.

faqs.q: Do I need to probate before selling an inherited house in Bryan?
faqs.a: Usually, unless another recorded route shows who has authority. Choices include a muniment of title, a small estate affidavit or an administration.

faqs.q: What can I do if a Bryan foreclosure sale is scheduled?
faqs.a: Move before the first Tuesday sale. You can reinstate within 20 days of the default notice, sell the house, or talk to the servicer about alternatives. After an auction, leftover equity goes to junior lienholders before it reaches you.
